_note: Weekly editorial. Update every week: "moving" = 3-4 stories moving markets, "trending" = 4 stocks explained. Owners, politician and insider activity are added automatically from the data.

moving.title: AI spending worries hit Big Tech again
moving.text: The Nasdaq fell 2.6% on Thursday, its biggest one-day drop since June, after Meta’s results showed AI spending pushing its free cash flow negative. Chip-equipment stocks fell with it. For the week the S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped, while the Dow and small caps finished higher.

moving.title: Oil climbs on Middle East attacks
moving.text: Brent crude rose to its highest level since late April after attacks in Saudi Arabia raised fears of more supply disruption. Energy stocks hit a record high on Friday, and the 10-year Treasury yield stayed near 5%.

moving.title: SpaceX shakes up wireless stocks
moving.text: AT&T and T-Mobile each fell more than 6% on Friday after a report that SpaceX is seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth US wireless carrier. Tower owners rose instead: Crown Castle gained 10% and American Tower 3.7%.

moving.title: Next week: the Fed and three tech giants
moving.text: The Federal Reserve announces its rate decision on Wednesday and is expected to hold. Microsoft and Alphabet report the same afternoon and Amazon on Thursday, a big test of whether AI spending is paying off.

trending.title: Meta drops nearly 7% after earnings
trending.happened: Meta fell about 7% on Thursday, closing near $649, after its third-quarter report. Revenue grew about 26% to roughly $64.6 billion, but heavy spending on AI data centres pushed free cash flow negative, and profit included a large one-time legal charge.
trending.means: Investors now want proof that AI spending turns into cash, not just revenue growth. Meta’s ad business is still growing fast, so the debate is about how much it spends, not whether the business works.
trending.note: Bill Ackman (about 9% of his portfolio) and Chase Coleman (about 7%) are among the 7 fund managers we track who own Meta.

trending.title: IBM rises as delayed deals close
trending.happened: IBM’s third-quarter revenue rose 4.7% to $17.1 billion, ahead of estimates, and it raised its software growth outlook to about 7% to 8%. Software deals delayed last quarter started to close. Shares rose about 4% in after-hours trading.
trending.means: It suggests big companies are still buying software, even while investors worry about AI spending elsewhere. Steady, cash-generating tech looked more attractive than heavy spenders this week.
trending.note: None of the 22 fund managers we track own IBM in their latest 13F filings.

trending.title: AT&T falls on SpaceX wireless report
trending.happened: AT&T and T-Mobile each fell more than 6% on Friday and Verizon fell 1.6%, after a report that SpaceX is looking for thousands of cell sites to launch a fourth wireless carrier.
trending.means: Wireless is a mature business where three carriers share most customers. A well-funded new rival could mean price cuts. Tower companies could gain, since a new carrier would rent space on their towers.
trending.note: None of the 22 fund managers we track own AT&T in their latest 13F filings.

trending.title: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report next week
trending.happened: Microsoft and Alphabet report third-quarter results after the close on Wednesday, 28 October, and Amazon on Thursday, 29 October. Analysts expect Microsoft to earn about $4.71 a share.
trending.means: After Meta’s drop, investors will focus on cloud growth and how much each company plans to spend on AI next year. Strong cloud sales could ease worries; bigger spending plans without matching revenue could add to them.
trending.note: 6 of the fund managers we track own Microsoft, including Bill Ackman, for whom it is about 12% of the portfolio.
